This will bring certain real estate income and gains into UK tax, while providing for unique access to Real Estate Investment Trusts for investments in UK real estate.

Writing down allowances – The government will introduce legislation in Finance Bill 2026-27 to increase the main rate first-year allowance to 50% for expenditure incurred on or after 1 January 2027 and to reduce the main rate writing down allowance to 12%, with effect from 1 April 2027 for Corporation Tax and 6 April 2027 for Income Tax.

Increase in rate of the Bank Corporation Tax surcharge for a temporary period – The government will temporarily increase the surcharge rate to 6% for 15 months, from 1 January 2027 to 31 March 2028, returning to 3% from 1 April 2028. This measure will be legislated for in Finance Bill 2026–27.

Improving R&D Tax Reliefs – The government will remove the R&D tax credit Claim Notification Form from 1 April 2027, and simplify the Additional Information Form from autumn 2027. The removal of the Claim Notification Form will be introduced through Finance Bill 2026-27, and changes to the Additional Information Form made through secondary legislation.

Increase Trading Allowance – The government will increase the Trading Allowance from £1,000 to £3,000, allowing individuals to receive up to £3,000 of trading and miscellaneous income tax-free each year. This will be introduced through Finance Bill 2026-27 and will take effect from 6 April 2027.

Enterprise Management Incentives 2 – The government will increase the Company Share Option Plan (CSOP) individual option limit from £60,000 to £120,000, remove the interaction with the Enterprise Management Incentive (EMI) option limit, allowing eligible employees to receive the full amount of options available under each scheme and extend the CSOP exercise period from 10 to 15 years. To help businesses understand how the schemes fit together, CSOP will be known as EMI2, reflecting its role as an option for growing companies that have moved beyond EMI or are not eligible for EMI. The government will also strengthen guidance and compliance activity on excessive fees, and engage with stakeholders on improving the Advance Assurance service.

Capital Gains Tax (CGT) Founders’ Relief – The government will introduce a new Founders’ Relief, providing a 10% CGT rate on up to £10 million of lifetime gains for qualifying founders of high-growth, innovative companies from 6 April 2027. Shares and share options set aside for employees will be able to be held for 15 years without triggering disguised remuneration rules. The changes will be introduced in Finance Bill 2026-27 and will take effect from 6 April 2027.

Improving Capital Gains Tax exit charge treatment for trusts affected by trustee migration –The government is making changes to capital gains legislation to provide an administrative easement to the ‘exit charge’ that otherwise applies when a trust ceases to be resident in the United Kingdom. The government will introduce legislation in Finance Bill 2026-27 which will have effect in relation to exit charges on or after 28 October 2026.

8. Financing

This annex sets out the government’s financing plans for 2026-27, which were previously revised on 23 April 2026.[footnote 176] Further details of the revised financing remit for 2026-27, including progress against the remit to date, can be found on the website of the UK Debt Management Office (DMO).[footnote 177] The government’s debt management framework remains as set out in the ‘Debt Management Report 2026-27’.[footnote 178]

8.1 Debt management objective

The debt management objective, as set out in the Debt Management Report 2026-27, is “to minimise, over the long term, the costs of meeting the government’s financing needs, taking into account risk, while ensuring that debt management policy is consistent with the aims of monetary policy.”

8.2 Debt management policy

The government’s decisions on the structure of the financing remit are made in accordance with the debt management objective, the debt management framework, and wider policy considerations. In determining the overall structure of the financing remit, the government assesses the costs and risks of debt issuance by maturity and type of instrument. Decisions on the composition of debt issuance are also informed by an assessment of investor demand for debt instruments by maturity and type, as well as the government’s appetite for risk. The government also takes into account the practical implications of issuance (for example, the scheduling of operations throughout the year).

Whilst decisions on debt management policy must be taken with a long-term perspective, specific decisions on funding the government’s gross financing requirement are taken annually. Those decisions are announced in advance of the forthcoming financial year and are typically updated in April (a technical adjustment to reflect outturn data from the previous financial year) and, as now, when the Office for Budget Responsibility (OBR) publishes updated fiscal projections.

HM Treasury, the Bank of England and the DMO have been developing a model whereby all Asset Purchase Facility (APF) active gilt sales are made to the government and not to the market. HM Treasury would instruct the DMO via the Debt Management Account to purchase the APF gilts that the Bank Executive is selling as part of its implementation of the Monetary Policy Committee’s (MPC’s) multi-year plan. HM Treasury would in due course instruct the DMO to issue a corresponding amount of debt to finance such APF purchases through the annual financing remit. As set out in the Chancellor’s letter to the Governor published on 17 September 2026, this model remains under review, such that, subject to a final decision to proceed, implementation could begin in a way that allows this to be incorporated into the DMO’s 2027-28 annual financing remit, as set by HM Treasury ministers.[footnote 179]

The planned split of gilt issuance by type, maturity and issuance method was previously set out in April 2026. Total gilt sales in 2026-27 are forecast to be £250.6 billion, which is £4.4 billion more than in the April 2026 remit revision.

8.4 Treasury bills

The April 2026 remit revision planned for Treasury bill issuance to make a £5‑billion net contribution to the 2026-27 NFR. Issuance of Treasury bills will now make a net contribution of £8 billion for 2026-27.

The government published in May 2026 a response to its consultation on expanding and deepening the UK Treasury bill market. Today, the government is providing further detail around the implementation of the measures it announced earlier in the year. The DMO has also confirmed several operational parameters in a press notice published today on its website.

Tenders for Treasury bills around the 12-month maturity point will begin in January 2027. The DMO will hold tenders for 12-month maturity Treasury bills initially every four weeks. The exact dates of Treasury bill tenders, including 12-month maturity tenders, taking place in Q4 2026-27 will be confirmed in the DMO’s Q4 2026-27 Treasury bill tender calendar announcement, due to be published at 11:30 am on Thursday 24 December 2026. The frequency of subsequent 12-month maturity tenders will be confirmed at future quarterly Treasury bill tender calendar announcements.

The Treasury Bill Standing Repo Facility (TBSRF) will open in January 2027 with the exact start date to be confirmed in the DMO’s Q4 2026-27 Treasury bill tender calendar announcement. The DMO is, from 28 October 2026, ready to work with Treasury Bill Primary Participants to complete the documentation required to access the TBSRF. Operational details about the TBSRF will be published in the relevant Terms and Conditions at the launch of the facility, but the DMO has announced the expected price, which will be kept under review, in a press notice published today on its website.

A collateral pool comprising £250 million (nominal) of each Treasury bill currently in issue as of 28 October 2026 has been created. Eligible DMO cash management counterparties can transact in the repo market with the DMO to borrow these securities. To maintain this collateral pool in future, the DMO will create a fixed amount of collateral for each Treasury bill at the point when it is issued for the first time at tender. The DMO does not intend to create collateral routinely at subsequent re-openings of existing Treasury bills. Collateral in the form of specific Treasury bills will be available to the market immediately following creation and will not be subject to an exclusive Delivery-by-Value holding period.[footnote 182] The fixed amount of collateral created for each Treasury bill instrument will be kept under review and will be confirmed in the DMO’s Treasury bill tender calendar announcement each quarter. These arrangements will be reflected in the Exchequer cash management remit, which will be published in the Debt Management Report 2027-28.

8.5 Green gilts and green retail savings products

The government continues to be committed to its Green Financing Programme, under which the UK issues sovereign green bonds (‘green gilts’) via the DMO, and retail Green Savings Bonds (GSB) via NS&I. As of 28 October 2026, the Green Financing Programme has raised more than £51.0 billion for expenditures that tackle climate change, rebuild natural ecosystems and support jobs in green sectors.

The government’s plans to raise £12.0 billion via issuance of green gilts in 2026‑27, subject to demand and market conditions, remain unchanged. Total green gilt proceeds in the financial year to-date are £6.3 billion (cash).

GSB were brought on sale on 22 October 2021 and have allowed UK savers to support the government’s green spending initiatives. As of October 2026, NS&I forecasts it will have raised £2.1 billion since the launch of GSB.

Financing raised through GSB is monitored throughout the year to ensure the requirements of the Green Financing Programme can be met and that funds raised remain balanced against proceeds from green gilts. For 2026-27, an inflow target of £500 million is in place, and revisions to the target are made to manage inflows into the Green Financing Portfolio and NS&I’s financing position. Based on current assumptions, NS&I forecasts £97 million of inflows against £510 million of outflows, resulting in a net funding forecast of -£413 million over 2026-27. NS&I will continue to keep the interest rate on GSBs under review.

8.6 Digital gilt instrument

At Mansion House, on 14 November 2024, the government announced the intention to launch a pilot digital gilt instrument (DIGIT) issuance. DIGIT will be an entirely new, digitally native, UK government debt instrument, issued onto a Distributed Ledger Technology (DLT) platform, and will support the government’s commitment to maintain the UK as a world-leading and global financial centre.

DLT refers to a variety of technologies characterised by their use of networks of ledgers that update and synchronise simultaneously. The DIGIT issuance will take place in the Digital Securities Sandbox (DSS) that allows UK firms to deliver DLT services within a sandbox regulatory environment. With this pilot, the government is seeking to explore how DLT can be applied across the lifecycle of the debt issuance process and catalyse the development of DLT in UK financial markets.

In October 2025, HM Treasury issued a tender notice to procure the services of a DLT supplier for the DIGIT issuance. Following a competitive process, HSBC, through its HSBC Orion platform, was announced as the government’s DLT supplier by HM Treasury on 12 February 2026. The government announced in February that Ashurst LLP are providing legal services for the DIGIT pilot. On 6 October 2026, following a competitive procurement process, Barclays, HSBC, Lloyds Bank Corporate Markets, Morgan Stanley, NatWest and RBC Capital Markets were appointed as the Joint Lead Managers for the DIGIT pilot issuance.

On 14 July 2026, the government confirmed that HSBC and London Stock Exchange Group (LSEG) have signed a memorandum of understanding to deliver a bilateral Digital Securities Depository (DSD) link. This link is the first of its kind in relation to a sovereign DLT issuance and is intended to provide connectivity between HSBC Orion DSD and LSEG’s DSD to support connectivity and investor access to the pilot issuance.

The government also confirmed that the DIGIT pilot issuance is expected to take place by the end Q1 2027.
